preamble: Debuccalization of the alveolar implosive: [ɗ] loses its oral closure and only the glottal component survives as [ʔ]. Gravina (2014) notes that Proto-Central Chadic *ɗ "is frequently reduced to /ʔ/ or lost altogether" in the modern languages, and the change shows up in several Central Chadic groups. Before *w the result is often labialized [ʔʷ] (Bata, Daba, Sukur and Higi ʔʷa 'breast'). That is a fusion of ɗ and w and is not counted among the examples here.

examples.note: Gravina (2014: 250), table (181). Mofu, Maroua and Lamang keep ɗɨwa(h).
Gravina (2014: 240), table (148). Tera ɗʲɨm keeps ɗ.

sources: Gravina, R. (2014). The Phonology of Proto-Central Chadic: The Reconstruction of the Phonology and Lexicon of Proto-Central Chadic, and the Linguistic History of the Central Chadic Languages. PhD dissertation, Leiden University (LOT). https://hdl.handle.net/1887/30139
